# Sandboxes on a GitHub repository

Five ways to work on a codebase in a sandbox. Each one starts from a
GitHub repository given as `owner/name` or `https://github.com/owner/name`.

## Where the GitHub token goes

`tritonctl` reads the token from `gh auth token`, or from a local
variable you name with `--github-token-env VAR`. It never takes a token
as a flag value.

- The token goes into the guest only in the environment of one git exec
  that moves objects: `clone`, `fetch`, `push` and `ls-remote`. Other git
  commands get no token. `pull` checks files out, which can run a filter
  the checkout names, so it gets none: run `fetch`, then `merge`.
- git reads it through a credential helper set for `https://github.com`
  only. A remote or submodule on another host gets no token.
- Those execs run with git hooks, the fsmonitor and a custom ssh command
  turned off.
- The token is not in the argv, the remote URL, a guest file, the
  sandbox create, its labels or metadata. The control plane does not
  store or log an exec environment.
- `sandbox pr` opens the pull request from your machine. Claude Code in
  the sandbox never gets the token.

What this cannot stop: while that exec runs, another process of the
same guest user can read its environment, and git's own output (which
you see) is the guest's to write. Use a fine-grained token for
the one repository, with contents and pull request write access only.

## 1. Clone and run

```sh
tritonctl sandbox create --name dev --repo owner/app --branch main
tritonctl sandbox exec dev --cwd /work/app -- make test
```

`--repo` clones into `/work/NAME` as the sandbox user once the sandbox
runs. It also adds the `github` network preset: `github.com`,
`*.github.com`, `*.githubusercontent.com` and `codeload.github.com`. Add
other names with `--allow-out-domain`, for example `pypi.org`.
`--net github` adds the same preset without a clone.

## 2. Claude Code on the repository

```sh
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
tritonctl sandbox claude --repo owner/app
```

This uses the sandbox `claude-app`, made on first use. The sandbox may
reach the Anthropic API and GitHub, and nothing else. The repository is
cloned on first use, and `claude` starts in `/work/app`.

## 3. Push and open a pull request

```sh
tritonctl sandbox git dev -- config user.name "Your Name"
tritonctl sandbox git dev -- config user.email you@example.com
tritonctl sandbox git dev -- switch -c fix-typo
tritonctl sandbox git dev -- commit -am "Fix a typo"
tritonctl sandbox pr dev --title "Fix a typo" --draft
```

`sandbox git` runs in the only checkout under `/work`; give `--repo-dir`
when there is more than one. Put the git subcommand first.
`sandbox pr` pushes the current branch to `origin`, opens the pull
request against the default branch (or `--base`), and prints its URL.
The title defaults to the last commit's subject.

## 4. VS Code Remote-SSH

```sh
tritonctl sandbox ssh-config dev --install
ssh dev.sandbox.triton
```

`ssh-config` makes a key pair for this sandbox on your machine, adds the
public key to the guest's `sandbox` account, starts sshd on the guest's
loopback, and pins its host key. The entry's `ProxyCommand` is
`tritonctl sandbox port-forward --stdio`, so ssh rides the same
authenticated tunnel as every other port. `--install` writes
`~/.ssh/tritonctl/dev.sandbox.triton.conf` and an `Include` line at the
top of `~/.ssh/config`; without it the entry is printed.

In VS Code, run "Remote-SSH: Connect to Host" and pick
`dev.sandbox.triton`. The guest allows local port forwarding, which VS
Code needs, and refuses passwords, root and agent forwarding.

## 5. A repository template, and many copies of it

Build a template with the toolchain:

```dockerfile
FROM rust:1
WORKDIR /work
```

```sh
tritonctl sandbox template build rust-dev --dockerfile Dockerfile --follow
tritonctl sandbox create --name app-warm --template rust-dev --repo owner/app
tritonctl sandbox exec app-warm --cwd /work/app -- cargo build
tritonctl sandbox snapshot create app-warm --name built
```

Then either make a template from the warm snapshot, for new sandboxes
anywhere:

```sh
tritonctl sandbox template build app --from-snapshot app-warm/built --wait
tritonctl sandbox create --template app --net github
```

or fork copies of it on the same host, each with the clone and the
build cache already there:

```sh
tritonctl sandbox fork app-warm --from-snapshot built --count 4 --name-prefix app
```

A copy made after `ssh-config` shares the guest's sshd host key. Take
the snapshot before you run `ssh-config`, or accept that the copies share
one host key.
